strengths: GIL correctly released in all 4 methods via py.detach()
py_dict_to_vanta_metadata handles all 4 types (String, Int, Float, Bool) — best metadata parser among adapters
filter_documents correctly honors top_k parameter (unlike other adapters with hardcoded limits)
Minimal dependencies — vantadb + pyo3 only, no extras
weaknesses: count_documents() truncates at default list limit (100) — only returns up to 100 records
Metadata inconsistency: write_documents drops non-string values but filter_documents (py_dict_to_vanta_metadata) handles all types
Does NOT implement true Haystack Document protocol — accepts/returns raw dicts, not haystack.dataclasses.Document objects
Test coverage thin (7 tests, no error paths, no real Haystack pipeline test)
comparison: Cleanest adapter structurally (201L, 4 methods, no extras). But the most significant design gap: unlike openai/ollama/litellm which implement real protocol interfaces, this adapter is 'Haystack-shaped' but not compatible with actual Haystack pipelines due to dict-level instead of Document-object I/O.
